Here is the assembled pump. The spout is on the left, the handle extends to the right, and the parts are stacked vertically on the base plate.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1376 768">
  <use href="#kit-base_plate" transform="translate(454.5,652)"/>
  <use href="#kit-pump_body" transform="translate(674.8,252.8) rotate(70)"/>
  <use href="#kit-cap" transform="translate(463.9,278.5) rotate(-55)"/>
  <use href="#kit-spout" transform="translate(349.18,614.88) rotate(-125)"/>
  <use href="#kit-link_bar" transform="translate(740.32,288.4) rotate(-160)"/>
  <use href="#kit-handle_lever" transform="translate(558.39,97.18) rotate(-35)"/>
  <use href="#kit-piston_rod" transform="translate(468.39,392.63) rotate(-70)"/>
</svg>

**How the parts fit:**
- **Base and body:** The base plate stays upright with its ground line at y=740. The pump body stands on the base's raised boss, centred at x=600. Its rounded chamber end sits at the bottom and the plain cylinder runs upward, so the piston rides inside the straight cylinder section.
- **Cap:** The cap's bottom plate sits centred on the body's top flange. Its lug, with two holes stacked vertically, sits on the right side.
- **Fulcrum link:** The link's lower hole pins to the upper lug hole on the cap. The link leans up and to the right at about 19° from vertical.
- **Handle:** The handle's small middle hole pins to the top of the link. Held level, this puts the handle's large end hole exactly over the cylinder centre line (x≈600). The grip end extends right and downward.
- **Piston rod:** The rod's top hole pins to that end hole, and the rod hangs vertically on the body's centre line. The piston sits inside the cylinder.
- **Spout:** The spout's large mounting flange sits flat against the left side of the body, just below the top flange. The tube runs left, then curves down to the outlet rim.

**Two choices the kit does not settle:**
- **Which lug hole:** I chose the upper cap lug hole for the link, because with the lower hole the handle end would sit on the cap dome.
- **Spout height:** The body has no marked seat for the spout, so its height is my best estimate rather than a matched feature.
